issues.title: Closed fixed-epsilon target bound
issues.failure_explanation: The prose and table claim bounds for C_ap,ε={z:r_F(z)≤ε}. The grids accept only h<ε-1/n. Uniform convergence and grid density approximate points where r_F<ε and hence the regularized target R_ap,ε=closure({r_F<ε}); they do not provide nearby accepted points for a point with r_F=ε that is not in that closure. No old hypothesis asserts C_ap,ε=R_ap,ε. Thus the proof supports a different target from the one stated.
issues.overall_effect: The fixed-ε bounds 2 and 1 are not established for the closed target. They apply to the regularized strict-sublevel target; the closed target requires the additional outer limit shown in v2. The exact-spectrum bounds can be recovered directly from regularized targets.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the fixed-epsilon target into R_ap,ε = closure({z:r_F(z)<ε}) and C_ap,ε = {z:r_F(z)≤ε}. State the height-2 and height-1 bounds only for R_ap,ε; recover C_ap,ε from C_ap,ε = intersection_q R_ap,ε+2^{-q}, giving height 3 and 2 bounds, and recover the exact approximate point spectrum from intersection_q R_ap,2^{-q}, retaining its height 3 and 2 bounds. Any sharpness assertion must likewise be restricted to the target for which it is established.
issues.why_classification: The strict residual grids prove convergence to the regularized target, not to all points of the closed level set. The target split and compact-intersection argument are contained, but they either replace the advertised fixed-epsilon target or worsen its SCI bound by one limit. This is a limited, recognizable weakening of a central guarantee rather than a routine no-loss correction.

issues.title: Unstable fixed-threshold inner set limit

failure_location.quote: Consequently, for each fixed $n_2$ the pointwise set-limit exists:

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed n_2, the old proof establishes h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)→h_{n_2}(z,F). If the limiting value equals the fixed threshold ε-1/n_2, the strict indicators may oscillate indefinitely, just as a convergent sequence t+(-1)^m/m alternates around t. Neither F2 nor the proof supplies monotonicity, a one-sided error, or threshold avoidance. Therefore the asserted finite-set limit does not follow from the numerical convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed arrays need not form the claimed inner discrete set limit, so the proposed type-G towers are not valid even for the regularized target until threshold stabilization is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the raw fixed-cutoff sets by a finite-grid threshold-stabilization construction. Applied to the convergent finite vector (h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)) over z in the grid, the construction must choose a cutoff within the existing O(1/n_2) slack so that every membership decision eventually stabilizes, while the limiting set remains sandwiched between the required nearby residual sublevels. The resulting inner limit and the subsequent outer Hausdorff argument must then be proved explicitly.
issues.why_classification: Scalar convergence does not justify convergence of strict threshold indicators at equality. Repairing this requires a genuine finite-dimensional threshold-selection lemma or equivalent construction, not a transcriptional edit, but the work is contained and can preserve the target, method, and tower-height guarantees without global reconstruction.

issues.title: Degenerate L1 dictionary directions
issues.failure_explanation: For X=[0,1], ω=δ_0, dyadic partitions whose positive-mass cell is tagged at 2^{-(n+1)}, and W=span{1,x}, every h_b(x)=1+bx has L1 norm one while Q_n(|h_b|)=|1+b2^{-(n+1)}|. The supremum of the quadrature error over b is infinite for every n. Thus the L1 unit sphere is not compact in the uniform norm because W contains the nonzero L1-null direction x, invalidating the proof and the universal statement.
issues.overall_effect: The old lemma does not establish assumption F2 for arbitrary finite-dimensional subspaces of C(X) when the measure lacks full support. Endpoint residual constructions need dictionaries interpreted in the L1 quotient with no nonzero null direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require each finite dictionary to inject into L1(ω), equivalently W intersect {h:||h||_1=0} = {0}, or formulate the dictionaries in the L1 quotient and choose finite-dimensional injective representatives. Then the L1 seminorm is a genuine norm on the coefficient space, its unit sphere is compact in the uniform norm, and the existing uniform quadrature argument applies. This retains arbitrary finite measures without imposing full support.
issues.why_classification: The proof uses norm equivalence where the L1 quantity may only be a seminorm. Quotienting out null directions or adding the standard finite-dimensional nondegeneracy condition is a short local repair that removes only redundant zero observables and does not alter the model class, residual target, rate, or algorithmic method.

issues.title: Impossible universal Borel-function evaluation coding

failure_location.quote: a Polish space of \textit{codes} $\mathsf{Code}(\X,\C)$ and a \textit{Borel evaluation map

issues.failure_explanation: Because X contains a Cantor subsystem, it is an uncountable standard Borel space. If a Polish code space and Borel evaluator represented every Borel characteristic function, choose a Borel isomorphism b from X onto the uncountable code space and form D={x:ev(b(x),x)=0}. This D is Borel and hence has a characteristic-function code c. At x=b^{-1}(c), the equality ev(c,x)=1_D(x) contradicts the definition of D. Thus the universal Borel evaluator used to make the witness relation Borel is nonexistent, and the projection argument does not establish analyticity.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that A_{z_0} is analytic and the analytic-completeness part of the reduction-route theorem are unsupported. A non-Borel conclusion would require only a valid hardness reduction, but that is logically weaker and separately affected by the Silver defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the impossible pointwise coding by the Polish space L0(ω) with convergence in measure, and take P = L0(ω)^N. On the Borel locus of continuous nonsingular maps, composition (F,f) ↦ f∘F is Borel: choose continuous L0-approximants Borelly from a countable dense family and use nonsingularity to pass their compositions to the L0 limit. Since the extended essential-supremum norm is Borel on L0, the set of (F,(f_n)) satisfying ||f_n||_∞=1 and ||f_n∘F-z_0f_n||_∞→0 is Borel, and its projection is A_{z_0}. This restores the analyticity input to the reduction-route theorem.
issues.why_classification: The universal Borel point-evaluator cannot be repaired, so the old proof must be replaced. Nevertheless, coding measurable equivalence classes in L0 gives a concrete, contained route to the same analyticity statement and preserves its dependent theorem. Establishing the Borel composition relation is substantial new reasoning but not global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Greedy Silver selector does not detect Silver subtrees

failure_location.quote: the pattern $u_m(S)$ has at least as many $\ast$-coordinates as

issues.failure_explanation: Let S consist of every finite word beginning with 1, together with the root and the dead level-one node 0. It contains the Silver tree obtained by fixing the first coordinate to 1 and leaving all later coordinates free. At level one the priority rule chooses the star because both 0 and 1 occur. At level two none of the three extensions of that star is admissible, so the recursion reaches bottom and all later star counts vanish. The associated finite-period map consequently has only bounded periods, and a non-torsion z_0 is not an approximate eigenvalue. Thus the asserted greedy maximality and the forward lemma are false.
issues.overall_effect: The Silver-tree spectral equivalence fails, so the analytic-completeness and type-G lower-bound chains based on that equivalence are not established. The actual pullback for this construction is Borel.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the stated finite-period construction, replace the Silver equivalence by the true Borel condition determined by unbounded selected periods and remove or materially downgrade every listed analytic-hardness and type-G lower-bound consequence. Retaining those consequences would require a fundamentally new tree-to-dynamics reduction that encodes coherent Silver witnesses rather than one greedily selected finite pattern; no such local replacement is established.
issues.why_classification: The counterexample destroys the core forward implication, and the resulting spectral pullback is Borel whereas the Silver-tree predicate is non-Borel. A local change of priority cannot preserve the recorded reduction chain: deleting the equivalence causes major loss throughout the listed conclusions, while recovering it requires essentially new reduction architecture.

issues.title: Undefined failure branch in the Lipschitz construction
issues.failure_explanation: The odometer is defined only for u in {0,1,*}^m, while the star-priority recursion explicitly outputs bottom when no extension works and remains bottom thereafter. For any such tree, the displayed update od_{m,u_m(S)} is outside its domain, so F_S and Ψ(S) are undefined despite the construction quantifying over every S.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed all-tree 1-Lipschitz map, its regularity lemma, its spectral formula, and the α-class corollary lack a defined input-output object on the failure branch.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the failure branch explicitly, for example by setting od_{m,⊥} to the identity permutation of 2^m and k(⊥)=0. Since failure persists at later levels, the corresponding blocks are then identity blocks. The map is defined for every tree and remains a measure-preserving 1-Lipschitz homeomorphism, with the spectral formulas interpreting those blocks as period one.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing branch rather than a uniquely forced typographical correction, but one routine local definition makes the construction executable on all inputs and leaves its regularity and intended spectral guarantees unchanged.

issues.title: Countable-block approximate-spectrum union formula

failure_location.quote: which exactly means $\lambda$ belongs to the closure of $\bigcup_j\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}(\K_{F|_{\mathcal X_j}})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Take blocks X_j={0,…,j} with F(k)=k+1 for k<j and F(j)=j, assign every atom positive measure, and form their countable disjoint union with finite total measure. Each finite-dimensional block Koopman operator has approximate point spectrum {0,1}. For λ=1/2, however, the unit vector f_j(k)=λ^k has residual only at the terminal point, of size (1-λ)λ^j→0. Hence λ belongs to the global approximate point spectrum although it is not in the closure of the union of the block spectra. The old proof's normalized vectors live in varying blocks and establish only that the corresponding lower norms tend to zero.
issues.overall_effect: The general countable-block spectral equality is false. Uses requiring its upper inclusion need a separate uniform resolvent estimate; finite- or two-block uses remain valid because the block infimum is then attained.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false union equality by the exact formula ν_F(λ)=inf_j ν_j(λ), hence σ_ap(K_F)={λ:inf_j ν_j(λ)=0}; only closure(union_j σ_ap(K_j))⊆σ_ap(K_F) holds in general. At every dependent use needing the reverse inclusion, supply a uniform blockwise lower bound. For the finite-period constructions, bounded periods give such a bound from finitely many resolvent formulas, while unbounded dyadic periods give a dense set of eigenvalues and the isometry confines the spectrum to the unit circle; finite and two-block uses retain the exact union formula.
issues.why_classification: The general lemma is mathematically false and its upper inclusion cannot be restored by a notation change. The exact lower-norm replacement and uniform-resolvent checks constitute a contained but nontrivial new argument across the affected uses, while preserving the finite-period spectral formulas and downstream guarantees attributable to this issue without global reconstruction.
